243:     """Return the tool declarations for the model prompt."""
244:     return [
245:         {
246:             "name": tool.name,
247:             "description": tool.description,
248:             "parameters": tool.input_schema,
249:             "level": tool.level,
250:         }
251:         for tool in TOOLS.values()
252:     ]

This looks **bounded** to the existing chat flow in `web/src/components/chat/` and `web/src/routes/ChatRoute.tsx` (with a forward-looking architectural note for cross-channel sandbox document delivery), so I will present the design right here in chat for your review before writing any code. ### Shared Understanding & Root Causes Identified 1. **Why the chat is overflowing and wrapping poorly:** - **Double `whitespace-pre-wrap` on Markdown (`BubbleContent` + `MarkdownContent`):** `BubbleContent` wraps `MarkdownContent` in `whitespace-pre-wrap`. In CSS, applying `pre-wrap` to the parent of parsed HTML blocks (`

`, `

    `, ``, `
    `) preserves source newlines between elements and prevents normal paragraph and flex/grid text reflow.
   - **Unconstrained flex children (`MessageItem` & `Bubble`):** In [`MessageItem.tsx`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/web/src/components/chat/MessageItem.tsx#L80-L103), `` is a flex row whose child lacks `min-w-0 max-w-full`, and the timestamp sits outside in a horizontal flex row without width clamping. When long URLs, inline code, tables, or math strings appear, the flex item expands past `100%` of the chat column.
   - **Hover scale overflow:** `hover:scale-[1.01]` on wide bubbles pushes them past the horizontal boundary of the container.

2. **Why the chat bubble & information showcase feel subpar:**
   - Assistant responses are currently stuffed inside a cramped muted bubble (`bg-[color-mix(in_srgb,var(--text)_7%,transparent)]`) with basic markdown spacing, no GFM (GitHub Flavored Markdown) plugin for tables/strikethrough/task lists, and no LaTeX math support.
   - While streaming ([`MessageStream.tsx`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/web/src/components/chat/MessageStream.tsx#L107-L113)), `streamedText` is rendered as raw unparsed text inside `BubbleContent` instead of through `MarkdownContent`, causing a jarring layout snap when the run completes.

3. **Why the thinking process feels flat:**
   - [`ThinkingCapsule.tsx`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/web/src/components/chat/ThinkingCapsule.tsx) renders every `tool_call` and `tool_result` as separate, disconnected generic list rows with raw JSON dumps, and doesn't recognize Vigil's actual tool suite (`exa_search`, `exa_contents`, `exa_find_similar`, `deliver_file`, `generate_document`, `ask_user`, `manage_tasks`, `skill_load`).

---

### Proposed Design

#### 1. Conversational Layout & Overflow Containment ([`MessageStream.tsx`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/web/src/components/chat/MessageStream.tsx), [`MessageItem.tsx`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/web/src/components/chat/MessageItem.tsx), [`bubble.tsx`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/web/src/components/ui/c-message-3-utils/bubble.tsx))
- **Strict Boundary Containment:** Enforce `min-w-0 max-w-full overflow-x-hidden` on the stream column and message rows, and `overflow-wrap: anywhere` (`wrap-anywhere`) on prose so long identifiers, URLs, or paths never bleed past the chat column.
- **Tactile User Bubbles (Right-Aligned):**
  - Clean, tailored pill/bubble (`max-w-[82%] sm:max-w-[75%]`, `rounded-[20px] rounded-br-[6px]`) using a subtle double-bezel hairline border (`border border-[var(--border)] bg-[color-mix(in_srgb,var(--text)_10%,transparent)] shadow-sm`).
  - Only user messages use `whitespace-pre-wrap break-words`.
- **Unboxed Editorial Assistant Replies (Left-Aligned):**
  - Following Vigil's design spec, assistant messages sit directly on the canvas (`w-full min-w-0`) without a claustrophobic outer box.
  - Heralded by a subtle header row featuring the inline Vigil spark mark, "Vigil" label, and hover timestamp.
  - Streaming replies render live through `MarkdownContent` with a smooth pulsing caret so there is zero layout jump when streaming finishes.

#### 2. Information Showcase & LaTeX Support ([`MarkdownContent.tsx`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/web/src/components/chat/MarkdownContent.tsx), `package.json`, `tokens.css`)
- **Dependencies:** Add `remark-gfm`, `remark-math`, `rehype-katex`, and `katex` (importing KaTeX CSS cleanly and overriding display math containers with `overflow-x-auto max-w-full py-2` so wide equations scroll internally instead of breaking the chat width).
- **Rich Typography & Elements:**
  - **Code Blocks:** Machined card header with language badge, line count, and tactile Copy button; `
    ` with `overflow-x-auto max-w-full`.
  - **Tables:** Wrapped in a rounded card shell with horizontal scroll (`overflow-x-auto max-w-full`), subtle header fill, and tabular numerals.
  - **Callouts / Blockquotes, Task Lists, & Links:** Polished spacing, custom list markers, external link indicators (`↗`), and balanced headings.

#### 3. Creative Card-Based Thinking & Execution Deck ([`ThinkingCapsule.tsx`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/web/src/components/chat/ThinkingCapsule.tsx))
- **Call + Result Pairing:** Group each `tool_call` with its matching `tool_result` (via `tool_call_id` or sequential pairing) into a single cohesive card with live status (`Running...` spinner → `Completed` emerald check / `Failed` rose badge) instead of two disconnected rows.
- **Connected Vertical Deck:**
  - A sleek outer capsule header showing live phase status, step counter badge, token count, and animated progress indicator.
  - Inside, a vertical timeline rail connects specialized cards for each step type:
    1. **Reasoning Card (`thought`):** Editorial quote card with token pill and collapsible full chain-of-thought.
    2. **Command Execution Card (`bash`):** Dark/sunken mini-terminal window with `$ command` prompt, status dot, and collapsible `stdout`/`stderr` output drawer with monospace scroll.
    3. **File Operation Card (`read`, `write`, `edit`):** Displays a file path pill, operation badge (`READ` / `WRITE` / `EDIT`), and expandable file snippet or diff preview.
    4. **Web & Knowledge Card (`exa_search`, `exa_contents`, `exa_find_similar`, `web_search`, `web_fetch`):** Search query pill and structured result links/snippets.
    5. **System & Skill Cards (`skill_load`, `manage_tasks`, `ask_user`, `approval_required`, `compaction`):** Purpose-built compact cards showing skill activation, task updates, or approval gates.
    6. **Sandbox Document Card (`deliver_file`, `generate_document`):**
       - Whenever the agent delivers a file or generates a document from the sandbox, it renders as a tactile **Document Artifact Card** (showing file format icon, filename, formatted byte size, SHA-256 fingerprint preview, and a preview/download action).
- **Historical & Live Persistence:** In [`ChatRoute.tsx`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/web/src/routes/ChatRoute.tsx) and [`MessageItem.tsx`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/web/src/components/chat/MessageItem.tsx), ensure the thinking deck sits cleanly above the assistant's reply while streaming and remains accessible via the step toggle on completed turns (and also enrich `mock.ts` so simulation mode showcases bash, file, search, document delivery, and LaTeX/GFM formatting).

#### 4. Future Consideration: Cross-Channel Sandbox Document Delivery
- I will add a concise architectural design note in `docs/sandbox-document-delivery.md` outlining how `deliver_file` / `generate_document` (which already emit `artifact_ref` and register rows in `/api/v1/artifacts`) can be bridged to any chat interface (Web Chat stream, Slack/Telegram/Email connectors) via an `artifact_delivered` step event and signed/authenticated download URLs.

---

110:         "jsonrpc": "2.0",
111:         "id": 1,
112:         "method": "tools/call",
113:         "params": {
114:             "name": tool_name,
115:             "arguments": arguments,

129:         headers=headers,

132:         with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as resp:
133:             body = resp.read().decode("utf-8")

# Cross-Channel Sandbox Document Delivery Architecture

## Overview
Vigil's sandbox harness includes two dedicated document delivery tools in `backend/src/modules/runs/tools/delivery.py`:
- `deliver_file`: Copies a file generated inside the ephemeral container (`/workspace/...`) to the host's delivery directory and computes its byte size and SHA-256 fingerprint.
- `generate_document`: Renders structured documents (`markdown`, `text`, `html`, `csv`) directly into the host delivery directory and returns an `artifact_ref`.

In the Web Chat UI (`ThinkingCapsule.tsx` / `SandboxDocumentCard`), tool calls and results for `deliver_file` and `generate_document` are paired into interactive **Document Artifact Cards** that remain pinned below the thinking summary even when the step trace is collapsed.

## Future Consideration: Universal Chat Interface Delivery

When extending Vigil so that sandbox documents can be delivered seamlessly to **any** connected chat interface (Web Chat, Mobile, Slack, Telegram, Discord, Email connectors), the following pipeline should be used:

### 1. Automatic Artifact Registration in `RunLoop`
Currently, `backend/src/modules/artifacts/router.py` exposes:
- `POST /api/v1/artifacts` (registers a run artifact row in the database)
- `GET /api/v1/artifacts/{artifact_id}` (metadata)
- `GET /api/v1/artifacts/{artifact_id}/download` (streams binary file with `Content-Disposition: attachment`)
- `GET /api/v1/artifacts/run/{run_id}` (lists all artifacts for a run)

In `RunLoop._write_tool_row` (`backend/src/modules/runs/loop.py`), whenever a tool returns a `ToolResult` with a non-null `artifact_ref`:
1. Persist an `ArtifactCreateDTO` record tied to `run.id` with `kind="delivery"`, `path=artifact_ref`, `size_bytes`, and an optional text `preview`.
2. Include `artifact_id` and `download_url: f"/api/v1/artifacts/{artifact_id}/download"` inside the `tool_result` step event payload.

### 2. Channel Adapter Dispatch
For external chat interfaces (or outbound connector actions):
- **Web & Mobile Native Clients:** Consume `artifact_id` from the `tool_result` step payload or `GET /api/v1/artifacts/run/{run_id}` and stream the binary file via authenticated `fetch` against `/api/v1/artifacts/{artifact_id}/download`.
- **External Messaging Connectors (Slack / Telegram / Email):** Subscribe to completed runs or expose a `send_artifact` connector capability that reads the registered `ArtifactDTO` stream from `ArtifactsRepository.get_artifact_stream(artifact_id)` and uploads it directly to the target thread or channel API.

This is a **bounded** race-condition bug in `POST /api/v1/runs/{run_id}/cancel` (`backend/src/modules/runs/service.py`) and `web/src/queries/chat.ts`.

### What Happened
When you clicked **Stop** in the chat composer, the worker had *just* finished the run (`status = 'completed'`) milliseconds earlier.
1. `cancel_run` in [`backend/src/modules/runs/service.py`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/modules/runs/service.py#L606-L615) unconditionally calls `update_run_status(run_id, status="failed")`.
2. Because `completed -> failed` is an illegal state transition in `RunStateMachine`, it threw `InvalidRunTransition`, which is not a subclass of `AppException`, causing FastAPI to crash with an unhandled `500 Internal Server Error` traceback in your logs.

### Proposed Fix (Short Design)
1. **Backend ([`backend/src/modules/runs/service.py`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/modules/runs/service.py#L606-L624)):** Make `_cancel_one` idempotent when the run has already reached a terminal state (`completed` or `failed`): if `RunStateMachine.is_terminal(current.status)` is true, return the existing run cleanly instead of attempting `completed -> failed` and crashing with an unhandled `InvalidRunTransition`.
2. **Frontend ([`web/src/queries/chat.ts`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/web/src/queries/chat.ts#L122-L126)):** Also check that `steps` does not already contain a `run_completed` or `run_failed` event when computing `streaming`, and guard `stop()` so it only fires if the run is not already terminal.

Shall I apply this fix?

yes.

Also, it seems that when the agent is running the states doesn't update properly until I refresh. And often when there is a connecting to VIGIL indicator that is always rolling even when nothing is happening. 1: """Resumable server-sent-event stream over the recorded run steps.
2: 
3: The stream is a cursor read. It asks the run step store for rows where
4: `step_number` is greater than the caller cursor, writes them, then polls again
5: after a short pause. A client that reconnects sends `Last-Event-ID` and receives
6: every later step exactly once. The stream holds no state between reads, so a
7: dropped connection loses nothing and a reconnected phone catches up.
8: """
9: from __future__ import annotations
10: 
11: import asyncio
12: import json
13: from typing import AsyncIterator
14: from uuid import UUID
15: 
16: from src.modules.runs.repository import RunStepDTO, RunsRepository
17: 
18: 
19: POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 0.5
20: """Pause between two cursor reads of the step store."""
21: 
22: KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 15.0
23: """A comment is written when no step arrived for this long."""
24: 
25: KEEPALIVE_COMMENT = ": keepalive\n\n"
26: """SSE comment that keeps an idle connection open. Clients ignore it."""
27: 
28: TERMINAL_RUN_STATUSES = frozenset({"completed", "failed"})
29: """The stream closes after the run reaches one of these statuses."""
30: 
31: SSE_HEADERS = {
32:     "Cache-Control": "no-cache",
33:     "Connection": "keep-alive",
34:     "X-Accel-Buffering": "no",
35: }
36: """Headers that stop a proxy from buffering or caching the stream."""
37: 
38: 
39: def parse_last_event_id(raw_value: str | None, fallback: int = 0) -> int:
40:     """
41:     Read the resume cursor from a `Last-Event-ID` header value.
42: 
43:     A missing header, a non-numeric value, and a negative value all fall back
44:     to the query parameter cursor.
45: 
46:     Args:
47:         raw_value: Raw header value, or None when the header is absent.
48:         fallback: Cursor to use when the header is unusable.
49: 
50:     Returns:
51:         A non-negative step number.
52:     """
53:     if raw_value is None:
54:         return max(0, fallback)
55:     text = raw_value.strip()
56:     if not text:
57:         return max(0, fallback)
58:     try:
59:         value = int(text)
60:     except ValueError:
61:         return max(0, fallback)
62:     if value < 0:
63:         return max(0, fallback)
64:     return value
65:

67: def format_sse_event(step: RunStepDTO) -> str:
68:     """
69:     Encode one run step as an SSE frame.
70: 
71:     The SSE id is the step number, so the client cursor is the same value that
72:     the next read compares against.
73: 
74:     Args:
75:         step: The run step to write.
76: 
77:     Returns:
78:         One SSE frame, terminated by a blank line.
79:     """
80:     data = json.dumps(
81:         {
82:             "run_id": str(step.run_id),
83:             "step_number": step.step_number,
84:             "event_type": step.event_type,
85:             "payload": step.payload,
86:             "created_at": step.created_at.isoformat(),
87:         }
88:     )
89:     return f"id: {step.step_number}\nevent: {step.event_type}\ndata: {data}\n\n"
90:

92: async def stream_run_events(
93:     store: RunsRepository,
94:     run_id: UUID,
95:     last_event_id: int = 0,
96:     poll_interval: float = POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS,
97:     keepalive_interval: float = KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL_SECONDS,
98:     max_duration_seconds: float | None = None,
99: ) -> AsyncIterator[str]:
100:     """
101:     Yield every run step after the cursor, then close when the run ends.
102: 
103:     The cursor moves only after a frame is written, so a step is never skipped
104:     and never sent twice. A read that returns no row writes a keepalive comment
105:     when the keepalive interval has elapsed.
106: 
107:     Args:
108:         store: Run step reader, normally the runs repository.
109:         run_id: UUID of the run to follow.
110:         last_event_id: Highest step number the client already has.
111:         poll_interval: Pause between cursor reads, in seconds.
112:         keepalive_interval: Idle time before a keepalive comment, in seconds.
113:         max_duration_seconds: Optional limit on the stream lifetime.
114: 
115:     Yields:
116:         SSE frames as text.
117:     """
118:     cursor = max(0, last_event_id)
119:     loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
120:     started_at = loop.time()
121:     last_write_at = started_at
122: 
123:     while True:
124:         steps = await store.get_steps_since(run_id, cursor)
125:         written = 0
126:         for step in steps:
127:             if step.step_number <= cursor:
128:                 continue
129:             cursor = step.step_number
130:             written += 1
131:             yield format_sse_event(step)
132:             last_write_at = loop.time()
133: 
134:         # A finished run closes the stream only after a read that returned no
135:         # new row, so a last step written just before the status change is
136:         # still delivered.
137:         run = await store.get_run_by_id(run_id)
138:         if written == 0 and run is not None and run.status in TERMINAL_RUN_STATUSES:
139:             return
140: 
141:         now = loop.time()
142:         if max_duration_seconds is not None:
143:             if (now - started_at) >= max_duration_seconds:
144:                 return
145:         if (now - last_write_at) >= keepalive_interval:
146:             yield KEEPALIVE_COMMENT
147:             last_write_at = now
148: 
149:         await asyncio.sleep(poll_interval)

252: def estimate_tokens(messages: Sequence[MessageDTO]) -> int:
253:     """
254:     Estimate the context size in tokens.
255: 
256:     The estimate is cheap and stable: four characters per token, plus a small
257:     constant per message. It is a gate for the compaction stage, not a bill.
258:

261: 
262:     Returns:
263:         The estimated token count.

265:     total = 0
266:     for row in messages:

### Root Cause Analysis: Live State Stalls & Perpetual "Reconnecting to Vigil..."

I traced the streaming pipeline end-to-end across [`sse.ts`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/web/src/lib/sse.ts), [`runs.ts`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/web/src/queries/runs.ts), [`chat.ts`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/web/src/queries/chat.ts), [`stream.py`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/modules/runs/stream.py), and [`loop.py`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/modules/runs/loop.py). You do **not** need WebSockets—SSE (`GET /api/v1/runs/{run_id}/events`) is the right architecture for unidirectional agent telemetry with `Last-Event-ID` resume, and the frontend isn't intentionally polling the API. Instead, **three bugs** are making SSE behave like a broken polling loop and stalling live state updates:

| Issue | Root Cause | File & Location |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. "Reconnecting to Vigil..." spins forever even when idle** | When a run finishes, the backend cleanly closes the HTTP response stream ([`stream.py`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/modules/runs/stream.py#L137-L139)). In [`createEventStream`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/web/src/lib/sse.ts#L108-L128), `reader.read()` returns `{ done: true }` and breaks out of the read loop—and **unconditionally calls `scheduleReconnect()`**! Worse, on reconnect the server responds `200 OK` (which resets `attempt = 0` at line 102) and immediately closes again because the run is already `completed`, trapping the browser in an **infinite 500ms reconnect loop forever** after every finished run. | [`web/src/lib/sse.ts`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/web/src/lib/sse.ts#L102-L129), [`web/src/queries/runs.ts`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/web/src/queries/runs.ts#L116-L142) |
| **2. Final run state & steps don't appear until page refresh** | In [`RunLoop._record_completion`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/modules/runs/loop.py#L1062-L1071) and [`_record_dispatch`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/modules/runs/loop.py#L1029-L1032), the worker updates `run.status` (`completed` / `awaiting_approval`) in its session, and in `stream_run_events` ([`stream.py`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/modules/runs/stream.py#L123-L149)) the API holds open a single SQLAlchemy `AsyncSession` transaction across every `while True` poll iteration without rolling back/ending the read snapshot (`session.expire_all()` / ending the transaction). 1. **Stop the Infinite SSE Reconnect Loop ([`web/src/lib/sse.ts`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/web/src/lib/sse.ts) & [`web/src/queries/runs.ts`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/web/src/queries/runs.ts)):**
